[Azure Bastion SKU comparison](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-sku-comparison), [Azure Bastion overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-overview)

finalExplanation: Azure Bastion Basic supports browser-based SSH connections to VMs in the same or directly peered virtual networks, but native RDP/SSH client connectivity requires the Standard or Premium SKU. VNet peering is nontransitive: a VNet1-to-VNet2 peering and a VNet2-to-VNet3 peering do not provide connectivity between VNet1 and VNet3. [Azure Bastion SKU comparison](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-sku-comparison), [Azure Bastion overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-overview)

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com.  
  
You plan to collaborate with a partner organization that has a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com.  
  
Fabrikam.com uses these identity providers:  
  
- Google Cloud Platform (GCP)  
- Microsoft accounts  
- Microsoft Entra ID  
  
You need to configure the Cross-tenant access settings for B2B collaboration.  
  
Which identity providers support cross-tenant access?

choices.label: B
choices.text: GCP and Microsoft Entra ID only

choices.label: C
choices.text: Microsoft accounts and Microsoft Entra ID only

choices.label: D
choices.text: GCP, Microsoft accounts, and Microsoft Entra ID

definition.explanation:
Cross-tenant access settings control B2B collaboration with external Microsoft Entra organizations. Google and Microsoft accounts are supported as external identity providers for guest sign-in, but cross-tenant access settings apply only to Microsoft Entra tenants.

**Learn more:** [What is Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/external-id/what-is-b2b)

finalExplanation: Cross-tenant access settings control B2B collaboration with external Microsoft Entra organizations. Google and Microsoft accounts are supported as external identity providers for guest sign-in, but cross-tenant access settings apply only to Microsoft Entra tenants.

definition.stemRaw:
After creating a new Azure subscription, you are tasked with ensuring that custom alert rules can be created in Azure Security Center.  
  
You have created an Azure Storage account.  
  
Which action should you take?

choices.label: A
choices.text: You should make sure that Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection is removed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You should create a DLP policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You should create an Azure Log Analytics workspace.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You should make sure that Security Center has the necessary tier configured.

definition.explanation:
Custom log-based alert rules require a Log Analytics workspace as the target data store for collected logs and queries. Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Azure Security Center) integrates with Log Analytics, and Azure Monitor creates custom log-search alert rules against that workspace.

**Learn more:** [View exported data in Azure Monitor - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/continuous-export-view-data) · [Log Analytics workspace overview - Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/log-analytics-workspace-overview)

finalExplanation: Custom log-based alert rules require a Log Analytics workspace as the target data store for collected logs and queries. Microsoft Defender for Cloud (formerly Azure Security Center) integrates with Log Analytics, and Azure Monitor creates custom log-search alert rules against that workspace.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company uses an Azure Container Registry.  
  
You must assign a user a role that permits uploading images to the Azure Container Registry. The assigned role must provide no more privileges than necessary.  
  
Which of the following roles should you assign?
definition.explanation:
The `AcrPush` role grants data-plane permission to push and pull container images and artifacts, without granting Azure resource-management permissions. `AcrPull` is limited to pulling images, while `Contributor` and `Owner` provide broader privileges than required.

**Learn more:** [Azure Container Registry Entra permissions and role assignments overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-registry/container-registry-rbac-built-in-roles-overview)

finalExplanation: The `AcrPush` role grants data-plane permission to push and pull container images and artifacts, without granting Azure resource-management permissions. `AcrPull` is limited to pulling images, while `Contributor` and `Owner` provide broader privileges than required.

You have an Azure subscription named Sub1.  
  
You create a virtual network containing one subnet. You provision the virtual machines on that subnet as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783952199313-m0vbkffk.png)  
  
No network security groups (NSGs) have been provisioned yet. You need to implement network security that meets these requirements:  
  
- Allow traffic to VM4 only from VM3.  
- Allow Internet traffic only to VM1 and VM2.  
- Minimize the number of NSGs and network security rules.  
  
How many NSGs and network security rules should you create?
definition.explanation:
One NSG attached to the subnet can use application security groups in its rules. Create an allow rule from AppGroup3 to AppGroup4, then a lower-priority deny rule from the virtual network to AppGroup4 so that the default AllowVNetInBound rule does not permit other VNet sources. A third rule allows Internet traffic to AppGroup12, which contains VM1 and VM2. The default inbound deny rule blocks Internet access to VM3 and VM4.

**Learn more:** [Application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/application-security-groups) · [Network security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/network-security-groups-overview)

finalExplanation: One NSG attached to the subnet can use application security groups in its rules. Create an allow rule from AppGroup3 to AppGroup4, then a lower-priority deny rule from the virtual network to AppGroup4 so that the default AllowVNetInBound rule does not permit other VNet sources. A third rule allows Internet traffic to AppGroup12, which contains VM1 and VM2. The default inbound deny rule blocks Internet access to VM3 and VM4.

You need to make sure that App1 can connect to VM1. The solution must minimize costs.

definition.explanation:
Regional virtual network integration lets an Azure App Service app make outbound connections to resources in a virtual network in the same region, including a VM running SQL Server. It avoids the virtual network gateway and associated cost required for gateway-required integration.

**Learn more:** [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration) · [Configure gateway-required virtual network integration for your app](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-gateway-required-vnet-integration)

finalExplanation: Regional virtual network integration lets an Azure App Service app make outbound connections to resources in a virtual network in the same region, including a VM running SQL Server. It avoids the virtual network gateway and associated cost required for gateway-required integration.

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy a new Conditional Access policy named CAPolicy1.  
  
You need to use the What If tool to evaluate how CAPolicy1 will affect users. The solution must minimize CAPolicy1's impact on users.  
  
What should you set the **Enable policy** setting for CAPolicy1 to?
definition.explanation:
Report-only mode evaluates and reports the outcome of a Conditional Access policy without enforcing its controls during sign-ins. It is included in What If evaluations, whereas a policy set to Off is not, so it permits impact assessment while avoiding disruption to users.

**Learn more:** [Troubleshoot Conditional Access Policies with the What If Tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/what-if-tool) · [Analyze Conditional Access Policy Impact](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ca/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-report-only)

finalExplanation: Report-only mode evaluates and reports the outcome of a Conditional Access policy without enforcing its controls during sign-ins. It is included in What If evaluations, whereas a policy set to Off is not, so it permits impact assessment while avoiding disruption to users.

You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You create an Azure web app named Contoso1812 that uses an S1 App Service plan.  
  
You plan to:  
  
- Create a CNAME DNS record for www.contoso.com that points to Contoso1812.  
  
You need to ensure that users can access Contoso1812 by using the https://www.contoso.com URL.  
  
Which two actions should you take? Each correct answer provides part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Turn on the system-assigned managed identity for Contoso1812.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Scale out the App Service plan of Contoso1812.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a deployment slot to Contoso1812.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Scale up the App Service plan of Contoso1812.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Upload a PFX file to Contoso1812.

definition.explanation:
An App Service custom domain must be added as a hostname on the web app after its DNS mapping is configured. HTTPS on that custom hostname also requires a TLS/SSL certificate bound to the hostname; a PFX file supplies a bring-your-own certificate. An S1 App Service plan supports the required SSL binding.

**Learn more:** [Overview of using custom domain names in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-custom-domains) · [Secure your domain with TLS/SSL in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-bindings)

finalExplanation: An App Service custom domain must be added as a hostname on the web app after its DNS mapping is configured. HTTPS on that custom hostname also requires a TLS/SSL certificate bound to the hostname; a PFX file supplies a bring-your-own certificate. An S1 App Service plan supports the required SSL binding.

definition.stemRaw:
You have 15 Azure virtual machines in a resource group called RG1.  
  
All of the virtual machines run the same applications.  
  
You need to stop unauthorized applications and malware from running on the virtual machines.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Apply an Azure policy to RG1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Azure Security Center, configure adaptive application controls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Identity Protection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Apply a resource lock to RG1.

definition.explanation:
Adaptive application controls use observed workloads to generate an allow list of known-safe applications for virtual machines and identify execution of applications outside that list. This application allow-listing capability is designed to protect machines from unauthorized software and malware.

**Learn more:** [Reference table for all compute security recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute) · [Azure security baseline for Virtual Machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/baselines/virtual-machines-windows-virtual-machines-security-baseline)

finalExplanation: Adaptive application controls use observed workloads to generate an allow list of known-safe applications for virtual machines and identify execution of applications outside that list. This application allow-listing capability is designed to protect machines from unauthorized software and malware.

You have an Azure Container Registry named `Registry1`.  
  
From Azure Security Center, you enable Azure Container Registry vulnerability scanning for the images in `Registry1`.  
  
You perform the following actions:  
  
- Push a Windows image named `Image1` to `Registry1`.  
- Push a Linux image named `Image2` to `Registry1`.  
- Push a Windows image named `Image3` to `Registry1`.  
- Modify `Image1` and push the new image as `Image4` to `Registry1`.  
- Modify `Image2` and push the new image as `Image5` to `Registry1`.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953697497-1njlra9m.png)  
  
Which two images will be scanned for vulnerabilities? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
Azure Security Center vulnerability scanning for Azure Container Registry automatically scans supported Linux images when they are pushed to the registry. Therefore, the Linux images `Image2` and `Image5` are scanned; the Windows images are not.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for container registries - benefits and features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-container-registries-introduction) · [Security considerations for container instances](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/container-instances/container-instances-image-security)

finalExplanation: Azure Security Center vulnerability scanning for Azure Container Registry automatically scans supported Linux images when they are pushed to the registry. Therefore, the Linux images `Image2` and `Image5` are scanned; the Windows images are not.

![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783953090039-0wz85rn4.jpg)  
  
RG1, RG2, and RG3 are resource groups. RG2 contains a virtual machine named VM2. You assign Azure role-based access control (RBAC) roles to the users shown in the following table.

statements.text: User1 can deploy virtual machines to RG1.

definition.explanation:
Azure RBAC assignments inherit from parent scopes to child scopes. Contributor assigned at the tenant root management group applies to RG1 and allows resource deployment. Virtual Machine Contributor assigned at Subscription2 applies to VM2 and allows VM deletion. Virtual Machine Administrator Login provides administrator login to a VM, but it does not provide the VM management permission needed to reset its local built-in Administrator password.

**Learn more:** [Understand scope for Azure RBAC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/scope-overview) · [Azure built-in roles for Compute](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/compute)

finalExplanation: Azure RBAC assignments inherit from parent scopes to child scopes. Contributor assigned at the tenant root management group applies to RG1 and allows resource deployment. Virtual Machine Contributor assigned at Subscription2 applies to VM2 and allows VM deletion. Virtual Machine Administrator Login provides administrator login to a VM, but it does not provide the VM management permission needed to reset its local built-in Administrator password.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure SQL database and implement Always Encrypted.  
  
You need to ensure that application developers can retrieve and decrypt data in the database.  
  
Which two pieces of information should you give the developers? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
Always Encrypted encrypts data with a column encryption key, which is itself protected by a column master key held in an external key store. An Always Encrypted-enabled client driver must be able to access the column master key to decrypt the column encryption key and return plaintext data. Developers therefore require the column master key and credentials that authorize its use.

**Learn more:** [Always Encrypted – How queries against encrypted columns work](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/always-encrypted-how-queries-against-encrypted-columns-work?view=sql-server-ver17) · [Create and store column master keys for Always Encrypted](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/create-and-store-column-master-keys-always-encrypted?view=sql-server-ver17)

finalExplanation: Always Encrypted encrypts data with a column encryption key, which is itself protected by a column master key held in an external key store. An Always Encrypted-enabled client driver must be able to access the column master key to decrypt the column encryption key and return plaintext data. Developers therefore require the column master key and credentials that authorize its use.

definition.stemRaw:
Your network has an on-premises Active Directory domain named adatum.com that synchronizes with a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
The Microsoft Entra tenant includes the users in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783965525016-tcvv04wa.png)  
  
You configure Microsoft Entra Password Protection for adatum.com as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783965527974-ejdly85x.png)  
  
For each statement, select **Yes** if it is true; otherwise, select **No**.

statements.text: User1 will be prompted to change the password on the next sign-in.
User2 can change the password to @d@tum_C0mpleX123.
User3 can change the password to Adatum123!.

definition.explanation:
Password Protection checks a password during a change or reset; it does not retroactively force a cloud-only user with an existing banned password to change it. The custom banned-password algorithm normalizes common substitutions and scores matched banned terms plus remaining characters; @d@tum_C0mpleX123 has sufficient remaining characters to meet the acceptance score. For on-premises AD DS, Audit mode records passwords that would be rejected but permits the password change, so Adatum123! is allowed.

**Learn more:** [Eliminate bad passwords using Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-password-ban-bad) · [Enable on-premises Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-ban-bad-on-premises-operations)

finalExplanation: Password Protection checks a password during a change or reset; it does not retroactively force a cloud-only user with an existing banned password to change it. The custom banned-password algorithm normalizes common substitutions and scores matched banned terms plus remaining characters; @d@tum_C0mpleX123 has sufficient remaining characters to meet the acceptance score. For on-premises AD DS, Audit mode records passwords that would be rejected but permits the password change, so Adatum123! is allowed.

finalExplanation: A single Azure Storage service endpoint covers access from its enabled subnet to multiple storage accounts, so storage1 and storage2 do not require separate endpoints. Azure Key Vault uses the separate Microsoft.KeyVault service endpoint. The Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory endpoint is a distinct endpoint type (used for Azure Data Lake Storage Gen1 integration). definition.stemRaw:
You must ensure that users are able to access VM0. The solution must satisfy the platform-protection requirements.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: B
choices.text: On Firewall, configure a network traffic filtering rule.

choices.label: D
choices.text: On Firewall, configure a DNAT rule.

finalExplanation: Just-in-time (JIT) VM access fails for a virtual machine that sits in a subnet whose route table forces outbound traffic through Azure Firewall as the next hop: the temporary inbound allow rule that JIT opens lets a connection reach the VM's public IP directly, but the return traffic is redirected to the firewall by the user-defined route, and the firewall drops it because it never saw the original inbound session — an asymmetric-routing failure. A network traffic filtering rule or a DNAT rule on the firewall does not fix this, because the problem is the asymmetric return path, not a missing allow or translation rule. Moving VM0 into a subnet that does not have the user-defined route pointing to the firewall removes the asymmetric-routing condition and lets JIT access function normally, while the firewall continues to protect the rest of the environment's traffic, satisfying the platform-protection requirement.

definition.explanation: Azure RBAC NotActions only carve out exclusions from the specific role definition they belong to; when a principal holds multiple role assignments, the effective permissions are the union of all assigned roles' allowed actions, so a delete permission granted by one role (Role2) is not blocked by a NotActions exclusion in a different assigned role (Role1) — this is why User2, who has both roles, can delete the VM even though User1, who has only Role1, cannot. Separately, Azure AD sign-in to a virtual machine is a data-plane operation controlled by dataActions (as used by the built-in Virtual Machine Administrator/User Login roles), and since both Role1 and Role2 have empty dataActions, no assignment of these roles grants the ability to log in to VM1 with Azure AD credentials.

definition.explanation:
Azure Key Vault separates a control plane (create/delete vaults, set access policies, configure network rules, and other vault properties such as purge protection) from a data plane (working with keys, secrets, and certificates). The control plane is authorized exclusively through Azure RBAC, while access policies (or RBAC data actions) govern only the data plane. The built-in Key Vault Contributor role grants control-plane management of a vault, including the ability to set access policies, without granting data-plane access to keys, secrets, or certificates - unlike Key Vault Reader, Network Contributor, or an Azure AD role such as Security administrator, none of which include the Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/write permission needed for vault property changes like purge protection or network configuration.

The control plane is authorized exclusively through Azure RBAC, while access policies (or RBAC data actions) govern only the data plane. definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You configure the subscription to use another Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) tenant.  
  
What are two possible effects of this change? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
> NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Role assignments at the subscription level are lost.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Virtual machine managed identities are lost.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Virtual machine disk snapshots are lost.

definition.explanation:
Changing a subscription to a different Azure AD tenant permanently deletes Azure RBAC role assignments from the source tenant, so subscription-level role assignments must be recreated. Managed identities associated with resources such as virtual machines do not transfer as functional identities; system-assigned identities must be re-enabled and user-assigned identities must be recreated. Existing Azure resources and their disk snapshots are retained.

**Learn more:** [Transfer an Azure subscription to a different Microsoft Entra directory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/role-based-access-control/transfer-subscription) · [Associate or add an Azure subscription to your Microsoft Entra tenant](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/fundamentals/how-subscriptions-associated-directory)

finalExplanation: Changing a subscription to a different Azure AD tenant permanently deletes Azure RBAC role assignments from the source tenant, so subscription-level role assignments must be recreated. Managed identities associated with resources such as virtual machines do not transfer as functional identities; system-assigned identities must be re-enabled and user-assigned identities must be recreated. Existing Azure resources and their disk snapshots are retained.

definition.stemRaw: Consider a Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) tenant with dynamic security groups, Group1 and Group2, whose membership rules are based on each user's City attribute. Select the membership that results for each group.

finalExplanation: Group1's dynamic membership rule uses the -contains operator (e.g., user.city -contains "ON"), which performs a case-insensitive substring search. Because the substring "on" appears somewhere in each of Montreal, MONTREAL, London, and Ontario regardless of letter case, all four users satisfy the rule and become members of Group1. Group2's rule uses the -match operator with a regular expression requiring the city value to end in the lowercase sequence "on" (e.g., user.city -match "on$"). Regular-expression matches in dynamic membership rules are case-sensitive for the pattern given, and only "London" ends with the exact characters "on"; Montreal ends in "eal", MONTREAL ends in "AL", and Ontario ends in "io". Therefore only User3 (London) qualifies for Group2. This illustrates the difference between the case-insensitive -contains operator and the case-sensitive regex behavior of -match in Microsoft Entra ID dynamic group rules.

definition.explanation:

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You create an Azure Firewall policy with the rules shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783964135786-u21bvey7.png)  
  
In what order should the rules be processed?
definition.explanation:
Azure Firewall Policy evaluates rule collection types in this fixed order: DNAT (NAT), network, then application. Rule collections of the same type are evaluated by ascending priority value. Thus NAT rules Rule2 (200) and Rule4 (400) precede network rules Rule3 (300) and Rule5 (500), followed by application rule Rule1 (100).

**Learn more:** [Azure Firewall rule processing logic](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/firewall/rule-processing)

finalExplanation: Azure Firewall Policy evaluates rule collection types in this fixed order: DNAT (NAT), network, then application. Rule collections of the same type are evaluated by ascending priority value. Thus NAT rules Rule2 (200) and Rule4 (400) precede network rules Rule3 (300) and Rule5 (500), followed by application rule Rule1 (100).

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that includes an Azure key vault.  
  
You create a storage account named storage1.  
  
You plan to store data in the following storage1 services:  
  
- Azure Files  
- Azure Blob storage  
- Azure Table storage  
- Azure Queue storage  
  
For which two services can you configure data encryption by using keys stored in the key vault? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
Azure Storage customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault protect Blob storage and Azure Files when configured for the storage account. Table and Queue storage require the storage account to have been created with an account-scoped encryption key before they can use customer-managed keys.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed keys for Azure Storage encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview) · [Create an account that supports customer-managed keys for tables and queues](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/account-encryption-key-create)

finalExplanation: Azure Storage customer-managed keys stored in Azure Key Vault protect Blob storage and Azure Files when configured for the storage account. Table and Queue storage require the storage account to have been created with an account-scoped encryption key before they can use customer-managed keys.

A separate database-level audit policy can run alongside server-level auditing, so DB2 writes to both configured destinations. Premium StorageV2 is not supported as the audit-log storage destination in this scenario.

definition.explanation:

definition.stemRaw:
You suspect that users are trying to sign in to resources for which they lack access.  
  
Create an Azure Log Analytics query that identifies failed user sign-in attempts during the last three days. The results must show only users with more than five failed sign-in attempts.  
  
How should you configure the query?
definition.template:
let timeframe = 3d;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(3d)
| where AccountType == 'User' and {{event_field}} == 4625

| summarize failed_login_attempts={{aggregate}}
latest_failed_login=arg_max(TimeGenerated, Account) by Account
| where failed_login_attempts > 5
definition.explanation:
Windows Security Event ID 4625 records a failed logon. Filtering AccountType to User limits results to user accounts, while count() aggregates failed-logon records for each account so the query can retain only counts greater than five.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Learn: Event 4625—An account failed to log on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4625)

finalExplanation: Windows Security Event ID 4625 records a failed logon. Filtering AccountType to User limits results to user accounts, while count() aggregates failed-logon records for each account so the query can retain only counts greater than five.

Authentication Administrator can view, set, and reset authentication methods for non-administrative users, while Privileged Role Administrator manages role assignments. Among the available roles, Global Administrator has the required tenant-wide administrative permissions. Microsoft Entra’s current role reference also distinguishes Authentication Administrator’s limited authentication-method scope from Global Administrator’s authority to manage all aspects of Microsoft Entra ID.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Create an AKS Ingress controller.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
An AKS Ingress controller routes inbound web traffic to services in an AKS cluster; it does not attach standalone Docker containers on a virtual machine to the virtual network. The Azure CNI plug-in is used to provide virtual-network networking to containers on a standalone Linux Docker host, allowing their traffic to originate through the subnet where the Azure Storage and Azure SQL service endpoints are configured.

**Learn more:** [Deploy container networking for a stand-alone Linux Docker host](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/deploy-container-networking-docker-linux) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

finalExplanation: An AKS Ingress controller routes inbound web traffic to services in an AKS cluster; it does not attach standalone Docker containers on a virtual machine to the virtual network. The Azure CNI plug-in is used to provide virtual-network networking to containers on a standalone Linux Docker host, allowing their traffic to originate through the subnet where the Azure Storage and Azure SQL service endpoints are configured.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: Install the container network interface (CNI) plug-in.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
The Azure Virtual Network CNI plug-in provides Docker containers with direct virtual-network attachment and virtual-network IP connectivity. Containers can therefore access Azure Storage and Azure SQL Database that are protected by service endpoints configured on the subnet.

**Learn more:** [Enable containers to use Azure Virtual Network capabilities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/container-networking-overview) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

finalExplanation: The Azure Virtual Network CNI plug-in provides Docker containers with direct virtual-network attachment and virtual-network IP connectivity. Containers can therefore access Azure Storage and Azure SQL Database that are protected by service endpoints configured on the subnet.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You create an application security group.  
  
Does the solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
An application security group only provides a logical grouping of network interfaces that can be referenced by network security group rules. It does not configure Docker container networking or enable container access to Azure Storage and Azure SQL through a virtual network service endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Network security groups and application security groups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/networking/design-guide/network-application-security-groups) · [Azure virtual network service endpoints](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-network/virtual-network-service-endpoints-overview)

finalExplanation: An application security group only provides a logical grouping of network interfaces that can be referenced by network security group rules. It does not configure Docker container networking or enable container access to Azure Storage and Azure SQL through a virtual network service endpoint.

definition.stemRaw: Which virtual networks in Sub1 can User9 modify and delete in their current state?

blanks.label: Virtual networks that User9 can modify:
Virtual networks that User9 can delete:

definition.explanation:
Azure resource locks take precedence over RBAC permissions. A CanNotDelete lock allows authorized users to read and modify a resource but prevents its deletion, while a ReadOnly lock prevents both modification and deletion (only read access remains). In this scenario, VNET1 resides in a resource group protected by a CanNotDelete lock, so User9 (who has adequate RBAC rights) can still modify it but cannot delete it. VNET2 and VNET3 reside in resource groups protected by ReadOnly locks, so User9 can neither modify nor delete them. VNET4 has no lock applied, so User9 can both modify and delete it. Consequently, the modifiable set is VNET4 and VNET1 only, and the deletable set is VNET4 only.

**Learn more:** [Lock resources to prevent unexpected changes - Azure Resource Manager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources)

finalExplanation: Azure resource locks take precedence over RBAC permissions. A CanNotDelete lock allows authorized users to read and modify a resource but prevents its deletion, while a ReadOnly lock prevents both modification and deletion (only read access remains). In this scenario, VNET1 resides in a resource group protected by a CanNotDelete lock, so User9 (who has adequate RBAC rights) can still modify it but cannot delete it. VNET2 and VNET3 reside in resource groups protected by ReadOnly locks, so User9 can neither modify nor delete them. VNET4 has no lock applied, so User9 can both modify and delete it. Consequently, the modifiable set is VNET4 and VNET1 only, and the deletable set is VNET4 only.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1.

You must ensure that Group1 members can stop, start, and restart the Azure virtual machines in Sub1. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

definition.explanation:
Azure custom RBAC roles are defined in JSON and created with New-AzRoleDefinition. A role containing only the VM start, restart, and stop/deallocate actions (and necessary read actions) follows least privilege. New-AzRoleAssignment then grants that custom role to Group1 at the Sub1 scope.

**Learn more:** [New-AzRoleDefinition](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.resources/new-azroledefinition?view=azps-15.4.0) · [New-AzRoleAssignment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.resources/new-azroleassignment)

finalExplanation: Azure custom RBAC roles are defined in JSON and created with New-AzRoleDefinition. A role containing only the VM start, restart, and stop/deallocate actions (and necessary read actions) follows least privilege. New-AzRoleAssignment then grants that custom role to Group1 at the Sub1 scope.

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com.  
  
A partner company has a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com.  
  
You need to ensure that, when a user in fabrikam.com tries to access resources in contoso.com, the user receives only one Microsoft Entra Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) prompt. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From the Azure portal of contoso.com, configure the inbound access default settings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the Azure portal of contoso.com, configure the External collaboration settings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the Azure portal of contoso.com, configure the outbound access default settings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From the Azure portal of fabrikam.com, configure the outbound access default settings.

definition.explanation:
Cross-tenant MFA trust is configured in the resource tenant's inbound cross-tenant access settings. When contoso trusts MFA claims from external Microsoft Entra tenants, it can accept MFA performed in fabrikam instead of requiring another MFA challenge. Configuring the inbound default settings provides this behavior with minimal administration.

finalExplanation: Cross-tenant MFA trust is configured in the resource tenant's inbound cross-tenant access settings. When contoso trusts MFA claims from external Microsoft Entra tenants, it can accept MFA performed in fabrikam instead of requiring another MFA challenge. Configuring the inbound default settings provides this behavior with minimal administration.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 with Security defaults disabled. The subscription includes the following users:  
  
- Five users who have owner permissions for Sub1.  
- Ten users who have owner permissions for Azure resources.  
  
None of the users have multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled.  
  
Sub1 has the secure score shown in the Secure Score exhibit. (Click the Secure Score tab.)  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783964139001-mkii0828.png)  
  
You plan to enable MFA for the following users:  
  
- Five users who have owner permission for Sub1.  
- Five users who have owner permissions for Azure resources.  
  
By how many points will the secure score increase after you make the planned changes?
definition.explanation:
The Enable MFA security control has a maximum score of 10 points. Protecting all five subscription Owners with MFA earns 5 points, and protecting five of the ten Azure-resource Owners earns half of the remaining 5 points, or 2.5 points. The total Secure Score increase is therefore 7.5 points. Microsoft documents that a control’s score is based on the score per resource multiplied by the number of healthy resources, and that Enable MFA has a maximum score of 10.

**Learn more:** [Secure score in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/secure-score-security-controls)

finalExplanation: The Enable MFA security control has a maximum score of 10 points. Protecting all five subscription Owners with MFA earns 5 points, and protecting five of the ten Azure-resource Owners earns half of the remaining 5 points, or 2.5 points. The total Secure Score increase is therefore 7.5 points. Microsoft documents that a control’s score is based on the score per resource multiplied by the number of healthy resources, and that Enable MFA has a maximum score of 10.

It does not supply inbound access to an app, so NSG1 on the integration subnet does not govern inbound traffic to WebApp1. An Isolated-tier App Service Environment is deployed in its VNet; WebApp2 can reach VM1 over the VNet peering. The default NSG VirtualNetwork rules include peered VNet address spaces and permit the traffic.

You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Key Vault Standard key vault named Vault1. Vault1 contains a 2048-bit RSA key named key1.  
  
You need to ensure that key1 rotates every 90 days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Modify the Access policies settings of Vault1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Upgrade Vault1 to Key Vault Premium.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Recreate key1 as an EC key.

definition.explanation:
Azure Key Vault key autorotation is configured per key by creating or setting a key rotation policy. The policy can specify a rotation interval of 90 days, which creates a new version of the existing RSA key. Key Vault Standard supports this capability; neither a Premium upgrade nor changing the key type is required. Managing the policy requires appropriate permissions, but modifying access policies alone does not configure rotation.

**Learn more:** [Configure cryptographic key auto-rotation in Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/how-to-configure-key-rotation) · [az keyvault key rotation-policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/keyvault/key/rotation-policy?view=azure-cli-latest)

finalExplanation: Azure Key Vault key autorotation is configured per key by creating or setting a key rotation policy. The policy can specify a rotation interval of 90 days, which creates a new version of the existing RSA key. Managing the policy requires appropriate permissions, but modifying access policies alone does not configure rotation.

choices.text: Modify the role-based access control (RBAC) role assignments for the root management group.

choices.label: B

definition.explanation:
Azure RBAC permissions are separate from Azure AD directory roles, so having Global Administrator rights in Azure AD does not automatically grant permission to manage resources, such as Blueprint definitions, at the management group scope. To author and save a Blueprint definition in the root management group, the account must first be granted an appropriate RBAC role (such as Owner or Blueprint Contributor) at that management group scope. Therefore, the necessary first step is to modify the RBAC role assignments on the root management group so the required permissions are in place before the Blueprint definition can be created there.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Blueprints - Azure Blueprints | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/blueprints/overview) · [How can I assign RBAC roles on the Tenant Root Management Group? - Microsoft Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/957054/how-can-i-assign-rbac-roles-on-the-tenant-root-man)

finalExplanation: Azure RBAC permissions are separate from Azure AD directory roles, so having Global Administrator rights in Azure AD does not automatically grant permission to manage resources, such as Blueprint definitions, at the management group scope. To author and save a Blueprint definition in the root management group, the account must first be granted an appropriate RBAC role (such as Owner or Blueprint Contributor) at that management group scope. Therefore, the necessary first step is to modify the RBAC role assignments on the root management group so the required permissions are in place before the Blueprint definition can be created there.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Export the public key from the on-premises server and save the key as a P7b file.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Export the private key from the on-premises server and save the key as a PFX file that is encrypted by using TripleDES.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Export the public key from the on-premises server and save the key as a CER file.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Export the private key from the on-premises server and save the key as a PFX file that is encrypted by using AES256.

definition.explanation:
An Azure App Service TLS/SSL binding requires a PFX certificate that includes the private key; public-key-only CER and P7B files cannot establish the server’s HTTPS identity. For the required PFX compatibility, export the certificate with its private key using TripleDES encryption. Microsoft’s App Service documentation notes that PFX files using AES256 can require overriding the cipher to use 3DES for App Service support.

**Learn more:** [Install a TLS/SSL certificate for your app in Azure App Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/configure-ssl-certificate)

finalExplanation: An Azure App Service TLS/SSL binding requires a PFX certificate that includes the private key; public-key-only CER and P7B files cannot establish the server’s HTTPS identity. For the required PFX compatibility, export the certificate with its private key using TripleDES encryption. Microsoft’s App Service documentation notes that PFX files using AES256 can require overriding the cipher to use 3DES for App Service support.

However, federation requires additional AD FS infrastructure and typically external-access proxy infrastructure, so it does not reduce the number of required servers.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect and federation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-fed-whatis) · [AD FS Password Attack protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/ad-fs/technical-reference/ad-fs-password-protection)

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You recommend using pass-through authentication and seamless SSO together with password hash synchronization.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Pass-through authentication enforces on-premises Active Directory account policies at sign-in, including disabled or locked accounts, password expiration, and permitted sign-in hours. It can be combined with Seamless SSO, and password hash synchronization may be enabled for backup or supporting features while pass-through authentication remains the primary sign-in method. finalExplanation: Azure selects routes from the source subnet using longest-prefix matching. The Vnet1-local route is more specific than Rt1's 0.0.0.0/0 route, so traffic between Subnet1-1 and Subnet1-2 stays within Vnet1. Vnet2-to-Vnet1 traffic uses the VNet peering system route; Rt2 is associated with Subnet1-2 and cannot affect traffic originating in Subnet2-1. You need to create an Azure key vault. The solution must ensure that any object deleted from the key vault is retained for 90 days.  
  
How should you complete the command?
definition.explanation:
Soft-delete retains deleted Key Vault objects for the configured retention period, which defaults to 90 days. Purge protection prevents a deleted vault or object from being permanently purged until that retention period elapses.

**Learn more:** [Azure Key Vault soft-delete](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/soft-delete-overview) · [New-AzKeyVault (Az.KeyVault)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/az.keyvault/new-azkeyvault?view=azps-15.3.0)

finalExplanation: Soft-delete retains deleted Key Vault objects for the configured retention period, which defaults to 90 days. Purge protection prevents a deleted vault or object from being permanently purged until that retention period elapses.

definition.stemRaw:
You have been tasked with delegating administrative access to your company's Azure key vault.  
  
You need to ensure that:  
  
- A specific user can set advanced access policies for the key vault.  
- Access is assigned based on the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which of the following options should you use to achieve your goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Key Vault management-plane operations, including configuring advanced access policies, are governed by Azure RBAC. By assigning the user an appropriate RBAC role (such as the built-in Key Vault Contributor role) scoped to just that key vault, you grant only the permissions needed to manage access policies, satisfying the principle of least privilege. Azure Information Protection handles data classification and labeling, not Key Vault access delegation; Azure AD PIM manages time-bound activation of already-granted roles rather than defining the access-policy permission itself; and Azure DevOps is unrelated to Key Vault permission management.

**Learn more:** [Assign a Key Vault access policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/assign-access-policy) · [Azure built-in roles for Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/security#key-vault-contributor)

finalExplanation: Azure Key Vault management-plane operations, including configuring advanced access policies, are governed by Azure RBAC. By assigning the user an appropriate RBAC role (such as the built-in Key Vault Contributor role) scoped to just that key vault, you grant only the permissions needed to manage access policies, satisfying the principle of least privilege. Azure Information Protection handles data classification and labeling, not Key Vault access delegation; Azure AD PIM manages time-bound activation of already-granted roles rather than defining the access-policy permission itself; and Azure DevOps is unrelated to Key Vault permission management.

The db_datareader and db_datawriter roles grant the required read and write permissions without the broader administrative permissions included in db_owner.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has an Azure subscription containing two virtual machines, VirMac1 and VirMac2, both in the **Stopped (Deallocated)** state.  
  
The virtual machines are in separate resource groups: ResGroup1 and ResGroup2.  
  
Two Azure policies have also been created, both configured for the `virtualMachines` resource type:  
  
- The policy for ResGroup1 uses the **Not allowed resource types** policy definition.  
- The policy for ResGroup2 uses the **Allowed resource types** policy definition.  
  
You then create a **Read-only** resource lock on VirMac1 and a **Read-only** resource lock on ResGroup2.  
  
Which statements are TRUE for this scenario? (Choose all that apply.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: You will be able to start VirMac1.

choices.label: B
choices.text: You will NOT be able to start VirMac1.

choices.label: C
choices.text: You will be able to create a virtual machine in ResGroup2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: You will NOT be able to create a virtual machine in ResGroup2.

definition.explanation:
A Read-only Azure resource lock allows only read operations and blocks modifications. Starting or restarting a virtual machine is a control-plane POST operation, so the Read-only lock on VirMac1 prevents it from being started. A Read-only lock at the resource-group scope prevents resource creation within that group; therefore, no virtual machine can be created in ResGroup2. An Allowed resource types policy permits the specified type but does not override a resource lock.

**Learn more:** [Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-resource-manager/management/lock-resources) · [Tutorial: Disallow resource types in your cloud environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/tutorials/disallowed-resources)

finalExplanation: A Read-only Azure resource lock allows only read operations and blocks modifications. Starting or restarting a virtual machine is a control-plane POST operation, so the Read-only lock on VirMac1 prevents it from being started. A Read-only lock at the resource-group scope prevents resource creation within that group; therefore, no virtual machine can be created in ResGroup2. An Allowed resource types policy permits the specified type but does not override a resource lock.

You have been assigned to apply Conditional Access policies for your company's existing Azure Active Directory (Azure AD).  
  
The process includes evaluating risk events and risk levels.  
  
Which risk level should be configured for sign-ins that originate from IP addresses showing suspicious activity?
